# Lab 5.6: SQL Stored Procedures

## What We Are Going to Do
Write a stored procedure with IN and OUT parameters and error handling, then call it from a script and from a scheduled query.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a target table and the procedure.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lab05.daily_sales (day DATE, orders INT64, revenue NUMERIC);

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE lab05.load_day(IN load_date DATE, OUT rows_written INT64)
BEGIN
  IF load_date &gt; CURRENT_DATE() THEN
    RAISE USING MESSAGE = FORMAT('Future date not allowed: %t', load_date);
  END IF;

  DELETE FROM lab05.daily_sales WHERE day = load_date;

  INSERT INTO lab05.daily_sales
  SELECT DATE(created_at), COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), CAST(SUM(sale_price) AS NUMERIC)
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items`
  WHERE DATE(created_at) = load_date
  GROUP BY 1;

  SET rows_written = @@row_count;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  SELECT @@error.message AS failed_with;
  SET rows_written = -1;
END;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Call it.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DECLARE n INT64;
CALL lab05.load_day(DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 DAY), n);
SELECT n AS rows_written;
CALL lab05.load_day(DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 5 DAY), n);
SELECT n AS rows_written_for_future_date;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The second call is caught by the exception handler and returns `-1`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| IN / OUT | Date in, row count out |
| Error handling | Bad input caught, returns `-1` |
| Idempotent | Delete then insert, safe to rerun |
| Scheduling | Procedure called daily with `@run_date` |
